mark 4 · 15% less time 345°F / 175°C Gas mark 4 · 10% less time What recipes use 200°C 200°C (392°F, gas mark 6) is the standard roasting setting for vegetables, potato wedges, chicken breast, sausages, salmon, homemade fries, and anything finished with a crisp edge. An air fryer is a roaster at heart, so this is where it most clearly beats the oven: a general recipe drops to 185°C, and fries take the largest time cut in the table because they have lots of surface and little depth. Notice the conversion never asks the basket to reach 200°C itself — the air fryer gets the same browning about 20% faster at a lower setting. The failure mode at 200°C: steamed, not roasted High heat in a small space only works if the moisture can get away. Cut vegetables and potatoes release water as they heat, and in a full basket that steam stays around the food, so instead of browning it softens and goes pale. It is the most common complaint about air-fried vegetables, and more time does not fix it. Cook in a single layer with gaps, or in two batches; the second batch is usually a minute or two faster because the basket is already hot. Dry vegetables well after washing, toss them in a teaspoon of oil rather than a spoonful, and shake the basket at the check time so the pieces at the bottom come up into the air. Worked example (conventional) A recipe roasts mixed vegetables at 200°C for 25 minutes. A basket air fryer does it at 185°C (365°F) in 19 minutes, with a shake at 13 minutes to check the colour. An oven-style air fryer takes 190°C (370°F) for 20 minutes; spread the vegetables over two racks and swap halfway. Worked example (fan) If the recipe gives 180°C fan, the same vegetables convert to 175°C (345°F) in a basket air fryer for 23 minutes, shake at 16 minutes. An oven-style unit runs 175°C (350°F) for 24 minutes. 200°C in °F and gas mark 200°C is 392°F (often rounded to 200°C on European dials) and gas mark 6. The air fryer setting is 185°C in a basket unit, 190°C in an oven-style one. If your air fryer only moves in 10°C steps, pick the lower step for vegetables and the higher one for chicken skin. Entering the recipe in °C in the converter gives you both numbers at once. For frozen packs, use the frozen mode. Nearby temperatures 180°C oven to air fryer → 220°C oven to air fryer → 400°F oven to air fryer → Oven to air fryer converter (any temperature) → Printable conversion chart → Frozen food mode (packaging instructions) → Convection oven to air fryer → Frequently asked questions What is 200°C in an air fryer? About 185°C (365°F) in a basket air fryer, with about 20% less time. In an oven-style unit, 190°C. Fries and bacon save the most time; baked goods take the smallest cut. My recipe says 180°C fan — is that the same as 200°C conventional? Yes, fan = conventional − 20°C. Use the fan input on this page for a fan-oven recipe; it takes a gentler cut. What gas mark is 200°C? gas mark 6. The UK dial marks 200°C as gas mark 6. Can I use this for a frozen food pack that says 200°C? No — frozen packs follow different rules (keep the temperature, cut 30% time). Use the frozen mode instead. Why are my air fryer vegetables soggy at 185°C? Almost always overcrowding. The steam from the vegetables cannot escape. Use a single layer, dry them well, use less oil; a hotter setting will not rescue a full basket.
